text:
maria_cs: Hey team, customer reporting intermittent JSON parse failures from our "json_mode" endpoint. They say sometimes keys from previous responses show up in the current response, e.g. {\"order_id\": 123, \"items\": [...], \"user_notes\": \"from-previous\"} where user_notes should never appear for this prompt. Happening for a small percentage of calls (~0.6%).

customer_janelle: repro attached — curl against hosted endpoint + small prompt. We get HTTP 200 but body is invalid JSON (trailing partial object or mixed fields). Happening with streaming on. Logs: \"parse_error: unexpected token at position 342\" and \"kv_cache_hit:1\" entries near the error. :frown:

sam_support: Thanks Janelle. Can you include the exact request payload (headers + body) and whether you use streaming=true or wait_for_full_response? Also which model/version and region?

customer_janelle: payload below, model: redwood/opt-low-latency:v2, region: us-east-1, streaming: true. We only see this in production under modest concurrency (~8 clients).

```json
{
  "input": "Generate order summary for order 9054 with items X",
  "structured": true,
  "json_schema": {"type":"object","properties":{"order_id":{"type":"number"},"items":{"type":"array"}}},
  "stream": true,
  "session_id": "acct-333-req-77"
}
```

jess_eng: Reproduced locally with a small parallel runner. Repro steps: run 50 parallel requests with short prefix + json_mode + streaming; after a few seconds ~0.4% responses show merged fields or truncated JSON. Minimal repro script (bash + jq):

```bash
seq 1 50 | xargs -n1 -P8 -I{} curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input":"Order summary {}","structured":true,"stream":true}' | jq . > out-{}.json &
wait
```

jess_eng: Output samples attached. In the bad responses I see a batch_id field in the token stream: "batch_id=btch-6" followed by tokens that include keys from a different request. Looks like a batching/prefix-cache interleave when concurrent requests have different prefix lengths. :eyes:

luca_eng_runtime: My hypothesis: prefix KV cache + continuous batching path is reusing KV state when a batch contains heterogeneous prefix lengths and streaming partial outputs are flushed/merged into another stream. The runtime currently reuses precomputed KV pages keyed by model+prefix_hash but there's a race window when cache fill/eviction and batch assembly happen concurrently. We saw similar races during early autotuner tests.

sam_support: Any quick mitigation we can apply for the customer? They're seeing user-impacting failures.

luca_eng_runtime: Short term: disable prefix caching for json_mode/structured=true on their tenant — that prevents KV reuse across requests, costs some throughput but should stop the leaks. Also disable streaming for affected route as a workaround (wait-for-full-response preserves per-request assembly). I'll prepare a flag toggle.

jess_eng: Created a repro ticket in runtime backlog with logs and sample bad outputs. Also adding a telemetry flag to emit batch_id, session_id pairs in the request logs to trace intermixing. Patch idea: make KV cache entries include a request-epoch nonce so they cannot be reused mid-batch.

deploy-bot: deploying runtime toggle for tenant acct-333 to disable prefix_cache for json_mode — rollout starting (canary 5% -> 100%).

maria_cs: Sent Janelle the temporary workaround (disable streaming or request toggle). She confirmed reduced failure rate immediately after canary. Thanks everyone. Follow-up: runtime team to ship fix and add an automated regression test covering parallel streaming + prefix-cache. :thumbsup:

jess_eng: Adding test to CI: run parallel streaming requests with mixed prefix lengths and assert schema compliance for 10k samples. Opening PR after triage.

luca_eng_runtime: Filed internal RFC for safe cache reuse semantics; will include locking/nonce approach. ETA for fix: ~2 weeks (hotfix in 4 days if we find small change).

maria_cs: Marking as escalated -> runtime bug. Will keep thread open until patch rolled out and verified in customer production.
